title_prefix: decodescript returns the pre-v22 shape a
mechanism: Our decodescript (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:964-1013) emits asm and type, then the pre-v22 reqSigs/addresses pair for multisig/pubkeyhash/scripthash, a segwit object containing ONLY an address for the three witness output types, and - unconditionally, outside every case branch - a p2sh address computed as hash160 of whatever script was passed. desc is never emitted and the singular address is never emitted. Core (refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:450-580) calls ScriptToUniv(include_hex=false, include_address=true) (core_io.cpp:409-428), which emits asm, desc, an optional singular address and type; reqSigs and addresses were removed in v22. It then computes can_wrap, which is FALSE for NULL_DATA, SCRIPTHASH, WITNESS_UNKNOWN, WITNESS_V1_TAPROOT and ANCHOR, and false again for a script that is unspendable, has invalid ops, or contains OP_CHECKSIGADD or an OP_SUCCESS; only then does it emit p2sh, and it emits the segwit object only under the further can_wrap_P2WSH test - which excludes every witness type and any multisig or pubkey carrying an uncompressed key. So our segwit object appears exactly where Core suppresses it and is missing exactly where Core produces it.
consequence: The p2sh field is the sharp end: we hand a caller a P2SH address wrapping an OP_RETURN, a P2SH address wrapping another P2SH, and a P2SH address wrapping a v1 taproot output. Anything paid to the first is unspendable, and the other two are redeemable by anyone who knows the redeem script, since the outer hash check is all that ever runs. Core deliberately stopped printing exactly these. A wrong address a client acts on: S2 by the rubric, with a loss path behind it if the address is ever paid to. The removed reqSigs/addresses and the missing desc break every consumer written against a current Core, and rpc_decodescript.py asserts the modern shape field by field.
evidence: Probe ga11v-rpcutil-p2 (scratch, not committed) *GA11-P2-DECODESCRIPT*, nine scripts through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method on a regtest node. OP_RETURN '6a0401020304' -> ((asm . 'OP_RETURN 01020304') (type . 'nulldata') (p2sh . '2NEVj61vjbUGuqGaBVK6YskrXUJyAdb81uM')) where Core emits asm, desc, type and NO p2sh. A p2sh script 'a914...87' -> type scripthash plus (addresses ...) plus a second p2sh '2N4T2kpWS7QghztV3LCW1qML2Aai9szNbT8'. A v1 taproot output '5120' + 32 bytes -> BOTH a segwit object (address bcrt1pzyg3...) and p2sh '2N2X7eTdkPj58YLGSSLYkDBaTzR4qrgJc8d'; Core emits neither and instead emits the taproot address itself. P2WPKH and P2WSH likewise carry a segwit object and a p2sh. The anchor script '51024e73' -> p2sh '2MxfMUdnrKwxjZDRzozhKk8UYsufbpwwgWg'; Core emits address bcrt1pfeesnyr2tx and no p2sh (rpc_decodescript.py:190-198, which asserts address bcrt1pfeesnyr2tx at :198). p2pkh -> (addresses ...) plural and p2sh but no segwit object, where Core emits the singular address, p2sh AND a full segwit object with asm/hex/type/address/desc/p2sh-segwit. No result carries desc, although tx-to-json's scriptPubKey does emit one (observed: 'raw(6a0400010203)#6scht25q' in the decoderawtransaction probe), so the field exists in the tree and only decodescript omits it. Ours: src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:964-1013. Core at d3056bc: rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:450-580; core_io.cpp:409-428; test/functional/rpc_decodescript.py:72-198.
fix_shape: Rebuild the handler as Core's: emit asm, then desc from the same descriptor inference tx-to-json already uses, then the singular address when a well-defined destination exists and the type is not PUBKEY, then type - and delete reqSigs and addresses. Port can_wrap verbatim, including the tail checks (HasValidOps, IsUnspendable, and a scan refusing OP_CHECKSIGADD or any OP_SUCCESS), and emit p2sh only under it. Port can_wrap_P2WSH as its own predicate and, under it, build the segwit script the way Core does - P2WPKH for PUBKEY and PUBKEYHASH, P2WSH otherwise - then render it through the same script-to-json helper with include_hex=true so the nested object carries asm, hex, type, address and desc, and append p2sh-segwit. The uncompressed-pubkey exclusion for MULTISIG and PUBKEY has to come along or a caller is handed a segwit address for a script that can never be spent under BIP143.
